errors_A: "its embedded schema's prose (system_context, writing_guidance, write_rules) is served as authoring guidance for that mem": false. render.rs build_schema_payload de-frames a third-party schema to the Lite skeleton regardless of requested verbosity (memstead-base/src/render.rs ~1712, OriginClass docs ~1547; query.rs schema_origin classifies any non-builtin schema not pinned by a writable mount as ThirdParty). The prose-instruction fields never reach the agent; a full request cannot re-admit them.
"Containment here is labelling, not filtering": overstated. Entity bodies are indeed only labelled, but the installed mem's schema prose IS filtered (see above).

Gap rather than error: "I could not verify that individual entity or search hits carry that marker": they do. memstead_entity stamps origin (binary: `entity ext--injected-concept --json` shows "origin": "third-party") and MCP search hits carry a per-hit origin (server.rs ~2385 and test entity_and_search_stamp_data_origin_by_mount_capability). The CLI search JSON does not show it.
errors_B: "Cross-mem relations inside the archive are stripped on load": wrong mechanism. The strict ingress validator refuses the archive at install (ValidationError::CrossMemRelationship; binary: `install crossmem2.mem` -> ARCHIVE_VALIDATION_FAILED "cross-mem relationship at injected-concept.md: target probe--local-note"). Stripping exists only on the export side (make_archive_self_contained), not at load.

"Each entity's authoring rationale travels with the archive": overstated. `.memstead/provenance.json` is an optional member (archive_provenance.rs, validator tolerates its absence); the test export of a folder mem carried none.
rationale: Both answers are well grounded: read-only mount, READ_ONLY_MOUNT on every mutation verb, Sealed backend, shadow-name refusal, strict validator (whitelist, symlink, zip-slip, drive-letter, caps), default-deny cross-mem policy with CROSS_MEM_TARGET_NOT_FOUND for read-only targets, third-party overview labelling, no MCP install tool, all verified by source and binary. A adds correct, useful limits (no download hash check, cross_linkable unenforced, schema staging). But A's central claim that the stranger's schema prose is served as authoring guidance is the opposite of the engine's de-framing, on the exact point the question asks about. B's only substantive slip is calling install-time refusal 'stripped on load'.
